Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

state noun

a country, a political community

also nation, the state, commonwealth, US state, federal state

classical

Cic. Amic. 23: quae tam firma cīvitās est
Traupman 180, 198
M-O s.v. political division: state

cīvitās, cīvitātis f.

noun, third declension

a state: its citizens as one body; one of the United States

The state as a community of citizens, from a city to a nation. Traupman and Morgan–Owens use it for each of the United States, Cīvitātēs Foederātae (Traupman 180).

Examples

  • quae enim domus tam stabilis, quae tam firma cīvitās est, quae nōn odiīs et discidiīs funditus possit ēvertī?

    for what house is so stable, what state so strong, that hatred and quarrels could not overturn it utterly?Cic. Amic. 23

  • America ex quot cīvitātibus cōnstat?

    How many states does America consist of?Traupman 198

Other words

  • rēs pūblica, reī pūblicae f. — the state, the commonwealth

    noun, fifth declension, with an adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.54: quasi sēminārium reī pūblicae

    The state as everyone’s concern, against private life: sī rē pūblicā nōn possīs fruī, stultum est nōlle prīvātā (Cic. Fam. 4.9.4, Lewis & Short).

  • status, statūs m. — condition, standing

    noun, fourth declension · avoid · classical · Traupman 180: Ūnītī Statūs, the United States

    A false friend: classically a condition, as in status reī pūblicae, the condition of the state, never the state itself (see state, condition).

See also state, government, political, America.
